experiment.schema:
CREATE TABLE experiment(
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  hypothesis TEXT, title TEXT, description TEXT,
  intervention TEXT, scope_skills TEXT, dataset TEXT,
  branch TEXT, worktree TEXT, commit_hash TEXT,
  status TEXT,
  baseline_win_rate REAL, result_win_rate REAL, lift_pp REAL, n_problems INT,
  merge_recommended INT,
  created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT, notes TEXT
)

rows.title: Active-pull consult_mental_model tool
rows.description: Gemini unique idea: on-demand tool instead of auto-injection. Architecture change; needs Class-B eval.
rows.notes: planned — intervention not yet implemented / needs Class-B (distractor) eval

rows.title: Capability-substitution: effort sweep (bayesian on medical)
rows.notes: slope of lift vs effort-rank = 0.00 pp/step → flat/no interaction. cells: low:+0pp, medium:+5pp, high:+5pp, max:+0pp. ISOLATION ON. CAVEAT: out-of-domain (medical), n=20/cell, none significant.

rows.title: Capability-substitution: model sweep (bayesian on medical)
rows.notes: slope of lift vs model-rank = 5.00 pp/step → COMPLEMENTS (helps more at high capability). cells: haiku:-15pp, sonnet:+0pp, opus:-5pp. ISOLATION ON. CAVEAT: generic Bayesian skill on out-of-domain medical MCQs; n=20/cell not significant. Directionally the guide HURT the weakest model (haiku -15pp) — opposite of substitution.

rows.title: In-domain capability ladder (skill vs placebo, 10 software/decision skills)
rows.notes: IN-DOMAIN (software/decision), pairwise, fixed judge gemini-3.1-pro-preview, isolation ON. slope=0.0pp/step → flat/no interaction. tiers: haiku:67%(p=0.1), sonnet:57%(p=0.584), opus:67%(p=0.1). POOLED across tiers: 57W/33L (n=90) = 63% beats placebo, 95% CI [53,73], p=0.015 SIGNIFICANT. Flat slope = constant lift across capability (no substitution). Contrast: out-of-domain medical HURT haiku — that was a domain-mismatch artifact. Isolated 63% > contaminated 56% → contamination had suppressed measured lift.

rows.hypothesis: Does circle-of-competence improve answer-vs-abstain calibration on SelfAware?
rows.title: circle-of-competence — abstention (n=70)
rows.description: Balanced 35/35 answerable/unanswerable; correct=answer-when-answerable & abstain-when-not.
rows.notes: p=0.773. No net effect; skill abstains slightly LESS on unanswerable (54% vs 60%). KILL/REWORK-leaning — does not improve calibration.

rows.title: bayesian correctness (authored base-rate MCQ)
rows.notes: INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING. placebo 98% (no headroom), skill 100%, Δ2.5pp p=1 n=40. Frontier model already at ceiling on textbook items → skill redundant at this difficulty; re-test with harder embedded items (placebo target 30-70%). HAIKU re-run also 100% placebo=skill (0 discordant) → ceiling across the haiku→sonnet ladder; the human failure mode is solved at textbook difficulty. Real verdict needs adversarially-hard embedded items.

rows.title: debiasing correctness (authored bias MCQ)
rows.notes: INCONCLUSIVE-CEILING. placebo 100% (no headroom), skill 98%, Δ-2.5pp p=1 n=40. Frontier model already at ceiling on textbook items → skill redundant at this difficulty; re-test with harder embedded items (placebo target 30-70%). HAIKU re-run also 100% placebo=skill (0 discordant) → ceiling across the haiku→sonnet ladder; the human failure mode is solved at textbook difficulty. Real verdict needs adversarially-hard embedded items.

rows.title: fermi-estimation correctness (jeggers/fermi, within-1-OOM)
rows.notes: KILL/REWORK. Isolated, judge-bias-free. skill 38% vs placebo 43% (Δ-5pp, McNemar p=0.724, n=40); trigger=43%=placebo. Full guide no better than placebo/trigger on objective Fermi estimation. Caveat: ns at n=40.

rows.title: first-principles — fundamental vs convention (n=30)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=0.479, near-ceiling (placebo 93%). ns; no reliable lift.

rows.title: map-territory — behavior contradicts docs (n=30)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=1.0. Ceiling (97%); skill redundant on clear contradictions.

rows.title: margin-of-safety — adequate buffer (n=30)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=0.248, ns. Headroom present (87%); skill did NOT help (−10pp, ns). No benefit.

rows.hypothesis: Does reworked fermi's +7.5pp@n40 hold at power (n=150)?
rows.title: fermi-estimation (reworked) — numeric OOM (n=150, POWERED)
rows.description: jeggers/fermi within-1-OOM, isolated, reworked skill.
rows.notes: p=1.0 (21 discordant), flat. The +7.5pp@n40 rework-rescue EVAPORATED to +0.7pp @n150 — it was small-N noise. Reworked fermi neutralized the old -5pp (no longer hurts) but adds NO measurable lift. Not an ELEVATE.

rows.hypothesis: Did the agent-native rework rescue fermi-estimation from its -5pp objective result?
rows.title: fermi-estimation (reworked) — numeric OOM (n=40)
rows.description: jeggers/fermi, within-1-OOM correctness, isolated. Reworked skill (When-NOT + decompose + don't-Fermi-lookupable).
rows.notes: p=0.371 (5 discordant), ns. But the rework FLIPPED the sign: old fermi was -5pp, reworked is +7.5pp (a ~+12.5pp swing). Directionally supports the rework recipe (cf. scientific-method). KILL downgraded to REWORK-RESCUED — confirm at n=150.

rows.title: occams-razor correctness (MedReason differential-dx, PROXY domain)
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (Δ+, ns). Isolated, headroom present (placebo 40%). PROXY domain (medical differential dx, not native software). placebo 40% skill 45% Δ5pp p=0.617 n=40.

rows.hypothesis: Does attacker-mindset (red-team) improve objective vuln detection on balanced data?
rows.title: red-team — DiverseVul balanced (n=80)
rows.description: Balanced 100/100 vuln/safe; Yes/No correctness, isolated, length-controlled.
rows.notes: McNemar p=0.052 — NEARLY significant, largest objective effect in the program. STRONG ELEVATE-leaning; confirm at n=150/200.

rows.title: red-team — DiverseVul balanced (n=200, POWERED)
rows.description: Full balanced 100/100 vuln/safe, Yes/No correctness, isolated.
rows.notes: p=0.10 (30 discordant), NOT significant. Regressed from +11.3pp p=0.052 @n80 -> +5pp ns @n200. Same shrink-at-power pattern as systems/five-whys. Directional positive (largest non-sci-method effect) but NOT a confirmed ELEVATE.

rows.title: reversibility — one-way/two-way (n=30)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=1.0. CEILING — model classifies door reversibility perfectly on clear cases; skill redundant. Needs borderline items for a real headroom test.

rows.hypothesis: Does cynefin improve ordered-vs-unordered problem classification?
rows.title: cynefin — classify (n=30)
rows.description: Authored balanced ordered/unordered; binary-decision.
rows.notes: p=1.0; placebo 97% (ceiling). INCONCLUSIVE-ceiling — model already classifies extremes correctly.

rows.hypothesis: Does socratic improve the clarify-or-proceed decision on ambiguous vs specified requests?
rows.title: socratic — clarify decision (n=29)
rows.description: Authored balanced clarify/proceed; binary-decision.
rows.notes: p=0.479; placebo near-ceiling (100%). No benefit; inconclusive (model already proceeds/clarifies well on clear-cut cases).

rows.title: scientific-method correctness (MedReason differential-dx, PROXY domain)
rows.notes: KILL/REWORK (headroom, no lift). Isolated, headroom present (placebo 48%). PROXY domain (medical differential dx, not native software). placebo 48% skill 43% Δ-5pp p=0.617 n=40.

rows.title: second-order — does action achieve goal w/ 2nd-order effects (n=30)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=0.617, ns. Headroom present (90%); skill did NOT help (slight negative). No effect.

rows.title: second-order — StrategyQA multi-hop (n=40)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=0.479. No effect on objective multi-hop. Confirms second-order null across two datasets.

rows.title: five-whys-plus SWE-bench fault localization (NATIVE software debugging)
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) NATIVE-DOMAIN. placebo 82% skill 89% Δ6.7pp p=0.248 n=45.

rows.title: five-whys-plus SWE-bench localization POST-IMPROVEMENT n=150
rows.description: Post-improvement SWE-bench fault localization check after trimming.
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) POST-IMPROVEMENT. placebo 82.0%, skill 85.3%, delta +3.3pp, p=0.131, discordant=7, n=150. Prior powered result was significant at +4.0pp.

rows.title: five-whys-plus SWE-bench localization POWERED n=150
rows.notes: ELEVATE (SIGNIFICANT) NATIVE-DOMAIN POWERED. placebo 83% skill 87% Δ4pp p=0.041 disc=6 n=150.

rows.hypothesis: Does five-whys-plus +4.0pp SWE lift replicate on a fresh n=150?
rows.title: five-whys-plus — SWE replication (n=150)
rows.description: Same current skill, fresh sample; SWE fault localization, isolated.
rows.notes: p=0.752. Does NOT replicate the +4.0pp (p=0.041). Another fragile borderline result. Only scientific-method (+9.3 p=0.002) remains robust.

rows.title: occams-razor SWE-bench fault localization (NATIVE software debugging)
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) NATIVE-DOMAIN. placebo 84% skill 89% Δ4.4pp p=0.617 n=45.

rows.title: occams-razor SWE-bench localization POST-IMPROVEMENT n=150
rows.description: Post-improvement SWE-bench fault localization check after trigger-scoping.
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) POST-IMPROVEMENT. placebo 82.7%, skill 84.7%, delta +2.0pp, p=0.505, discordant=9, n=150. Essentially unchanged from prior powered result.

rows.title: occams-razor SWE-bench localization POWERED n=150
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) NATIVE-DOMAIN POWERED. placebo 83% skill 85% Δ2pp p=0.45 disc=7 n=150.

rows.title: scientific-method SWE-bench fault localization (NATIVE software debugging)
rows.notes: no effect NATIVE-DOMAIN. placebo 84% skill 84% Δ0pp p=1 n=45.

rows.title: scientific-method SWE-bench localization POST-IMPROVEMENT n=150
rows.notes: ELEVATE (SIGNIFICANT) POST-IMPROVEMENT (audit edits applied). Δ9.3pp p=0.002 n=150. Prior: 0pp (was flat).

rows.title: scientific-method rework prototype SWE-bench n=150
rows.notes: Historical prototype evidence before replacing shipped scientific-method. Original was 0pp; prototype reached +5.3pp, p=0.061, n=150. The shipped skill now contains this hypothesis-differential approach.

rows.title: systems SWE-bench fault localization (NATIVE software debugging)
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) NATIVE-DOMAIN. placebo 80% skill 89% Δ8.9pp p=0.221 n=45.

rows.title: systems SWE-bench localization POST-IMPROVEMENT n=150
rows.notes: ELEVATE-leaning (ns) POST-IMPROVEMENT (audit edits applied). Δ3.3pp p=0.182 n=150. Prior: +5.3pp (was firm ELEVATE).

rows.title: systems SWE-bench localization (POWERED n=150)
rows.notes: ELEVATE (SIGNIFICANT) NATIVE-DOMAIN POWERED. placebo 80% skill 85% Δ5.3pp p=0.043 disc=12 n=150.

rows.hypothesis: Does restoring the trimmed leverage table recover systems' +5.3pp SWE lift?
rows.title: systems-restored — SWE replication (n=150)
rows.description: Leverage table restored; SWE fault localization, isolated.
rows.notes: p=0.683. Does NOT replicate the +5.3pp (p=0.043). Restoring content did not recover it — the original ELEVATE was fragile borderline noise. KEY: replicate before claiming.

rows.title: theory-of-constraints — bottleneck ID (n=30)
rows.description: isolated, length-controlled, judge-free binary/correctness
rows.notes: p=1.0. CEILING — model identifies the binding constraint from numbers on clear cases; skill redundant.

rows.title: Bifurcation: conceptual skills → trigger cards
rows.description: Replace verbose conceptual skills the model already knows with a 2-3 sentence trigger card; test trigger >= full file.
rows.notes: clean +25pp, no per-skill regression; aligns with committee #1 (verbose conceptual files are net-negative). Merge-ready pending powered re-run. Branch exp/exp-l1-0eadc0 [SUPERSEDED by paired-design re-run]

rows.title: Bifurcation: conceptual skills → trigger cards
rows.description: Replace verbose conceptual skills the model already knows with a 2-3 sentence trigger card; test trigger >= full file.
rows.notes: paired head-to-head, length-balanced, same-run. modified beats original 79% (n=12, 95% CI [56,98], p=0.046, SIGNIFICANT). commit 3b5bbfc23.

rows.title: LLM-native rewrite of human-artifact skills
rows.description: Strip human stage-directions, reframe around LLM failure modes, add stop conditions + no-fabrication guards.
rows.notes: net +12.5pp but MIXED: debiasing +67 / regret +33 helped, bayesian -17 / circle -33 regressed. Merge only debiasing+regret rewrites after a powered run. [SUPERSEDED by paired-design re-run]

rows.title: LLM-native rewrite of human-artifact skills
rows.description: Strip human stage-directions, reframe around LLM failure modes, add stop conditions + no-fabrication guards.
rows.notes: paired head-to-head, length-balanced, same-run. modified beats original 67% (n=12, 95% CI [41,93], p=0.289, directional). commit bf241fc0f.

rows.title: Procedural skills as executable checklists
rows.description: Convert procedural skills to inputs→steps→stop→answer-template; planned (needs intervention impl).
rows.notes: planned — intervention not yet implemented / needs Class-B (distractor) eval

rows.title: Universal "When NOT to use" boundaries
rows.description: Class-B: measurable only with an expanded distractor eval (off-target problems).
rows.notes: planned — intervention not yet implemented / needs Class-B (distractor) eval

rows.title: Consolidate 5 overlap clusters
rows.description: Merge unanimous clusters; mainly improves routing discrimination (Class-B).
rows.notes: planned — intervention not yet implemented / needs Class-B (distractor) eval

rows.title: Skill stacking: first-principles+second-order+red-team
rows.notes: length-controlled, isolation ON. stack beats placebo 78% (p=0.074), beats SINGLE skill 72% (p=0.221). directional synergy, n=9 underpowered.

rows.title: Post-skill verifier / reversion gate
rows.description: GPT unique idea: a no-framework verifier pass reverts framework-theater outputs. Harness change, not skill edit.
rows.notes: planned — intervention not yet implemented / needs Class-B (distractor) eval

experiment_result.schema:
CREATE TABLE experiment_result(
  experiment_id TEXT, skill TEXT,
  baseline_win_rate REAL, result_win_rate REAL, lift REAL, n INT,
  PRIMARY KEY(experiment_id, skill)
)
